global_issues.title: 10-Year Treasury Yield Hits Highest Since 2002
global_issues.note: The 10Y reached about 5.344% intraday, the highest since April 2002, and closed near 5.28% on Oct 2. The briefing's 'later partially reversed' is right for Oct 1, when yields retreated from the multiyear high. The yield rose about 4bp on Oct 2, so the easing was not sustained. The briefing is stale: it omits Oct 2 and the jobs report.

global_issues.title: Oil Surges Over 4% on Middle East Risks and China Export Halt
global_issues.note: The Oct 1 move is confirmed: Brent Dec settled at $102.31, up 4.4%, and WTI settled at $92.87. The cause is also confirmed: China suspended fuel exports beyond HK/Macau and a third US carrier is heading to the Middle East. On Oct 2 oil gave back ground. Brent fell about 3% intraday to roughly $99–102, and WTI fell 3.6% to about $89.5–92.6. Gulf exports are recovering and there is talk of diesel and crude stock releases. A reader would wrongly infer oil is still surging.

grok_report.summary: The Oct 1 facts are accurate: the 10Y hit its highest since 2002, oil rose over 4%, and the cause was the China fuel halt plus a third US carrier. The briefing misses the Oct 2 weak jobs report (+29k), the oil pullback and the fading Fed-hike expectations, so its mood and sector framing are stale. Individual stock prices could not be verified, and the MU price looks suspect.
